key_insight: Exponential moving averages used by Adam/Muon can be reformulated as training a linear regressor via online gradient flow, which enables approximating dense optimizer states with a low-rank factorization that preserves optimization dynamics while cutting memory.
problem_solved: The large memory overhead of first- and second-order EMA momenta in modern optimizers that limits model scale, batch size, and training efficiency during large-scale pre-training.
method: Reinterpret EMA momenta as coefficients learned by an online linear regressor (online gradient flow equivalence).
Factorize dense optimizer state matrices into low-rank components and update these factors online (LoRA-Pre) to emulate EMA behavior.
Apply the low-rank optimizer as a drop-in replacement during pre-training to reduce memory and compute with minimal impact on convergence.
impact: Significantly lowers optimizer memory footprint so practitioners can train larger models or use larger batches without extra hardware; provides a practical, memory-efficient optimizer alternative for LLM pre-training.
visual_elements: Schematic showing EMA ↔ online linear regressor equivalence (equation + intuitive diagram).
Before/after matrix visualization: dense optimizer states vs low-rank factorization (two small matrices).
Bar/line chart comparing memory use, throughput, and convergence (Adam/Muon vs LoRA-Pre).
Pipeline diagram showing LoRA-Pre as a drop-in optimizer in a standard pre-training workflow.
paper_title: Taming Momentum: Rethinking Optimizer States Through Low-Rank Approximation
paper_authors: Zhengbo Wang, Jian Liang, Ran He, Zilei Wang, Tieniu Tan
